sections.heading: Overview
content: This policy outlines Humana's criteria for items that are reimbursable as implantable devices.

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Subject to all applicable limitations, such as provider contract terms, a covered item may be eligible for specific reimbursement as an implantable device only when the item is of a type that is implanted, such as a piece of tissue, a tooth, a pellet of medicine, a tube or needle containing a radioactive substance, a graft, or an insert. Also included are liquid and solid plastic materials used to augment tissues or to fill in areas traumatically or surgically removed, stents, artificial joints, shunts, pins, plates, screws, and anchors. Humana may review documentation, including but not limited to, itemized bills, invoices, and medical records, to determine whether items reported with implant revenue codes meet Humana’s definition of an implantable device. Humana requires providers to make such documentation available to Humana upon request. Humana does not reimburse an implant revenue code if the item does not satisfy Humana’s definition of an implantable device.
